page: Microsoft Azure F64ads_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor operating up to 4.5 GHz. The instance provisions 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring one thread per core, alongside 256 GB of system RAM corresponding to 4.0 GB per core. The cache architecture provides 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. Vector and cryptographic acceleration is supported via AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and VAES instruction sets. Local ephemeral storage is bundled with a 7,560 GB NVMe SSD array, eliminating reliance on network-attached disks for high-bandwidth scratch storage.

Empirical benchmarks place the instance within the top decile across computational and memory workloads. In stress-ng evaluations, it registered 3,777.46 in single-core and 233,122.48 in multi-core metrics, matched by a PassMark CPU score of 114,652.97. Uncached memory read bandwidth achieved 416.51 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measured 205.45 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 170.73 million Redis SET operations per second and 99.57 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For CPU-based language model processing, small 135M parameter models process prompts at 5,672.85 tokens per second, while 7B parameter models sustain text generation at 63.72 tokens per second.

The 1:1 physical core mapping prevents thread contention, providing predictable execution times for compute-heavy workloads. The combination of 64 high-frequency cores and 7.56 TB of local NVMe storage provides strong resource density for distributed databases, high-throughput caching, continuous integration compilation, and batch data processing. However, the 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio and lack of dedicated GPU hardware make it less suitable for training large neural networks or memory-bound workloads exceeding 256 GB.
description: Microsoft Azure F64ads_v7 is a compute-optimized instance driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core and 256 GB of memory. It features 7,560 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage alongside support for AVX-512 and VAES instruction sets. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier for compute and memory bandwidth, recording a multi-core stress-ng score of 233,122.48, 416.51 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth, and 170.73 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-based inference yields 63.72 tokens per second on 7B parameter models, although throughput scales down on 70B parameter variants. By combining high clock speeds, dedicated core allocation, and fast local NVMe capacity, the instance is well suited for high-throughput batch compute, in-memory caching layers, large-scale web servers, and I/O-intensive database workloads.
